notes: One classification of every file the claude-native and codex-native harnesses write under the computer's home, from the fork's source (file:line in `evidence`) and checked by running the fork's own writers under a throwaway home (spikes/s6/followup/bridge_check.py).

Patterns are relative to the home directory, or to the temporary directory for root "tmp" (Claude-native's bridge lives in $TMPDIR/omnigent-<uid>/claude-native, outside the home; its rules apply only if $TMPDIR lies inside a checkpointed directory).

`*` matches within one path segment, `?` one character in a segment, `**` any number of segments. The first matching rule wins, so specific rules come first. A directory a rule saves is traversed, and each member is decided on its own; a directory a rule excludes is skipped whole.

Actions: exclude (never in a workspace checkpoint; stripped with an alert if found in a layer), save (continuation state), save-link (a symbolic link kept as a link, never followed), decide (saved today, but can hold a secret: the lead decides; RC-53 flags it).
Every family lists its temporary-write variants: a capture can pause between a write and its rename.

rules.evidence: inner/codex_executor.py:1180-1226 (symlink to ~/.codex/auth.json; copy2 fallback); app_server.py:2106-2114 relinks a missing one at every start
rules.why: A link (or a copied fallback) to the declared login file. Excluded by path whatever its type; the start relinks it. Codex rewrites auth.json in place (no temporary sibling).

rules.evidence: inner/codex_executor.py:1187, 1206-1216 (os.link: a hard link, same inode as ~/.codex/.credentials.json; copy2 fallback)
rules.why: A hard link: an archive that follows the path stores the whole MCP login. Must be excluded by path; the start re-links it.

rules.evidence: harnesses/codex_native/app_server.py:1547-1597 (a minimal private home with its own auth.json link, .credentials.json hard link and provider tables)

A restored state.json or startup error points turns at a dead app-server or fails them until relaunch; clear_bridge_state removes them at every launch anyway. The dead-letter .tmp files are transient rewrites; the queue itself is saved.

rules.evidence: inner/codex_executor.py:1252-1287 (copied from ~/.codex/config.toml), 2214-2268 and app_server.py:3784-3797 (an Omnigent key provider's auth command is printf %s '<key>': a literal API key); launch_args.py:450-507 (the profile copies whole tables)
fields: model_providers.*.auth.args (literal API key for Omnigent key providers)
rules.why: The session's private settings (/model, effort, trust, writable roots, developer instructions) must survive, so it is saved. With a subscription login it holds no secret; with an Omnigent key provider it holds the key in plain text. Lead decides: fork change (reference the key instead of inlining it), scrub on capture, or accept with an RC-53 exception.
